allObjections.title: Unbounded recommendation generation risk
allObjections.detail: The minimal envelope in §7 item #8 lacks any rate limits or caps on recommendation volume. Without PA-1..PA-N invariants, agents could flood operators with thousands of low-quality recommendations, creating noise that obscures critical findings.

allObjections.title: Cost estimation without validation
allObjections.detail: The new cost.effort_hours_estimate field has no validation bounds or methodology specified. Engineering could estimate '0.5 hours' for a cross-product migration or '1000 hours' for a button color change with no canonical guardrails.

allObjections.title: Rollback procedure underspecified
allObjections.detail: The rollback.revert_procedure is just an optional string with no structure. CA16A-v2-CT-3 only warns on non-revertable accepted recs but doesn't prevent accepting high-blast-radius changes with no documented rollback path.

allObjections.title: Defer window gaming vulnerability
allObjections.detail: The per-product defer window [1,365] allows operators to effectively suppress recommendations forever by setting 365-day deferrals. No mechanism prevents serial deferral abuse or tracks cumulative defer time.

allObjections.title: Lack of Rollback
allObjections.detail: The proposal does not provide a clear rollback mechanism for accepted recommendations, which could lead to unintended consequences. This is a concern in §7 item #8, where the minimal canonical envelope is defined.

allObjections.title: Insufficient Cost Estimation
allObjections.detail: The cost object in the minimal canonical envelope only includes effort hours estimate, risk tier, and blast radius, but does not account for other potential costs, such as resource utilization or opportunity costs, which could lead to inaccurate cost assessments.

allObjections.title: Overly Permissive Defer Window
allObjections.detail: The per-product defer-window config allows for a wide range of values (1-365 days), which could lead to inconsistent application of recommendations across products and potentially cause delays or inefficiencies in the implementation process.

allObjections.title: Ambiguous Target Classification
allObjections.detail: The stricter detection rules in §6 Multi-Format Targets may lead to an increase in `target_class_ambiguous` findings, causing unnecessary operator intervention and potential delays in the classification process.

allObjections.title: Defer-Window Complexity
allObjections.detail: The per-product defer-window config in §7 item #8 + §3 admin config adds complexity to the system. Operators may struggle to manage different defer windows for multiple products, leading to inconsistencies and potential mismanagement.

allObjections.title: Lack of Rollback Path
allObjections.detail: The proposal does not specify a clear rollback path for accepted recommendations that turn out to be problematic. This could lead to significant issues if a recommendation is accepted and later found to be detrimental.

allObjections.title: Overhead of Side-Channel Recommendations
allObjections.detail: Proactive recommendations being a side-channel creates additional overhead for operators who now have to manage and dispose of these recommendations asynchronously to the Clearance pipeline, potentially leading to increased workload and reduced efficiency.

allObjections.title: Incomplete Schema
allObjections.detail: The minimal envelope lacks critical fields and validation rules that were part of the v1 proposal, potentially leading to incomplete or inconsistent data.

allObjections.title: Ambiguity in Rollback
allObjections.detail: The new `rollback` object introduces ambiguity regarding what constitutes a'safely revertable' recommendation, which could lead to confusion in implementation.

allObjections.title: Overhead for Operators
allObjections.detail: The asynchronous disposal of recommendations outside the §11 Clearance flow may increase operational overhead for operators, as they will need to manage recommendations separately.

allObjections.title: Cost object underspecified
allObjections.detail: The `cost` object in the proactive recommendation envelope lacks specific guidance on how `effort_hours_estimate`, `risk_tier`, and `blast_radius` should be determined, leading to inconsistent application and potential gaming of the system. The lack of a canonical scale for `risk_tier` and `blast_radius` is particularly concerning.

allObjections.title: Rollback procedure ambiguity
allObjections.detail: The `rollback` object's `revert_procedure` field is optional and human-readable, which introduces ambiguity and potential for error. Without a standardized format or automated process for rollback, operators may struggle to effectively revert recommendations, especially in complex systems.

allObjections.title: Deferral window clamping
allObjections.detail: While the per-product defer-window config is a good idea, the clamping mechanism for out-of-bounds values, while notifying the admin, could still lead to unexpected behavior if the admin doesn't immediately correct the configuration. A more robust solution might involve preventing the setting of out-of-bounds values in the first place.

allObjections.title: Lack of versioning for recs
allObjections.detail: The proactive recommendation envelope lacks explicit versioning. As the system evolves and new recommendation types are introduced, the absence of versioning could lead to compatibility issues and difficulties in interpreting older recommendations.

allObjections.title: Cost object over-constraining
allObjections.detail: The `cost` object in the minimal envelope (§7 item #8) introduces a `risk_tier` and `blast_radius` which may over-constrain the recommendation process, especially for low-impact or experimental recommendations.

allObjections.title: Rollback mechanism insufficient
allObjections.detail: The `rollback` object (§7 item #8) only includes a boolean `revertable` and an optional `revert_procedure`. This may be insufficient for complex recommendations that require detailed rollback procedures to avoid unintended side effects.

allObjections.title: Per-product defer-window too flexible
allObjections.detail: The per-product defer-window (§7 item #8 + §3 admin config) allows a wide range of values [1, 365] days. This flexibility could lead to inconsistent operator behavior and make it difficult to manage recommendations across different products.

allObjections.title: Deferred schema is underspecified
allObjections.detail: In §7 item #8, the proposal defers PA-1..PA-N invariants to engineering dispatch while simultaneously making the minimal envelope canonical. That leaves validation gaps around category values, uniqueness of `id`, and cross-field constraints, so implementers can ship incompatible interpretations of the same SSOT contract.

allObjections.title: Rollback field is toothless
allObjections.detail: The new `rollback` object in CA-16-A v2 only records `revertable` and an optional human-readable `revert_procedure`. It does not require an executable rollback path, audit linkage, or automatic enforcement on acceptance, so it can create false confidence without preventing irreversible bad recommendations.

allObjections.title: Clearance bypass weakens governance
allObjections.detail: In CA-16-A-Q2 v2, proactive recommendations are moved entirely outside §11 Six-Step Clearance and the proposed Step 1.5 is eliminated. That creates a second governance lane with no gating relationship to readiness, which can let high-risk recommendations accumulate and influence operators without the same review standards as other release-critical items.

allObjections.title: Per-product window can fragment policy
allObjections.detail: CA-16-A-Q4 introduces `product_registry.recommendation_defer_window_days` with wide bounds [1,365]. This makes the resurfacing cadence a product-local knob, so fleets can drift into inconsistent operator experiences and missed follow-up on high-priority recommendations, especially when admins set long windows to suppress workload.

allObjections.title: Unclear Cost Estimation
allObjections.detail: The 'cost' object in §7 Proactive Recommendations envelope lacks clear guidelines for estimating 'effort_hours_estimate'. How will operators calibrate this?

allObjections.title: Defer-Window Config Risks
allObjections.detail: The per-product 'recommendation_defer_window_days' config has wide bounds [1,365]. What prevents operators from setting it too high, potentially ignoring critical recommendations for an extended period?

allObjections.title: §7 envelope omits regression guard
allObjections.detail: The minimal proactive_recommendation schema in §7 item #8 adds cost/rollback but never references the §7.6 post-deploy regression guard or the five Self-Renewal safety invariants; a recommendation that lowers gtm_readiness_score_delta can still be accepted without triggering agent.fix.regression_detected.v1.

allObjections.title: ClearanceRecord ignores recs entirely
allObjections.detail: §11 Six-Step Protocol and ClearanceRecord entity record only the six enumerated steps; the side-channel governance_record_entry for proactive_recommendation.v1 has no timestamp linkage to any ClearanceRecord step, so deferred recs can silently expire without updating the atomic ProductSSOT delta_log required by §7.5.

allObjections.title: defer_window bounds too permissive
allObjections.detail: product_registry.recommendation_defer_window_days accepts [1,365] with only clamping; a 365-day value on a high-velocity product violates the §28 symbiotic loop feedback assumption that recommendations re-surface within a single sprint cycle.

CA-16-A-v2-Q1.rationale: This preserves traceability to purpose when available while allowing flexibility for novel recommendations, addressing both the over-constraint and citation concerns.

CA-16-A-v2-Q2.rationale: Post-deploy surfacing ensures operators see recommendations without blocking clearance, while maintaining visibility within the canonical flow rather than relegating to a side-channel.

CA-16-A-v2-Q3.rationale: Rejected recommendations may become relevant as products evolve; allowing admin-gated reopening with rationale provides flexibility without cluttering the active queue.

CA-16-A-v2-Q4.pick_text: Ratify with admin role required for any value > 30 days; operator may set up to 30.
CA-16-A-v2-Q4.rationale: This prevents operators from indefinitely suppressing recommendations through extreme deferrals while allowing reasonable short-term postponement for legitimate resource constraints.

objections.detail: §11 Six-Step Protocol and ClearanceRecord entity record only the six enumerated steps; the side-channel governance_record_entry for proactive_recommendation.v1 has no timestamp linkage to any ClearanceRecord step, so deferred recs can silently expire without updating the atomic ProductSSOT delta_log required by §7.5.

objections.title: defer_window bounds too permissive
objections.detail: product_registry.recommendation_defer_window_days accepts [1,365] with only clamping; a 365-day value on a high-velocity product violates the §28 symbiotic loop feedback assumption that recommendations re-surface within a single sprint cycle.

adversarial.worse_than_status_quo: Operators accept non-revertable recommendations (rollback.revertable=false) that later trigger §7.6 regressions; because the envelope is minimal and schema is deferred, the system ships changes that the prior absence of proactive recs would have prevented, increasing rollback debt.

perReviewer.rejection_steelman: The v2 draft still embeds two new mutable objects (cost, rollback) and a per-product config knob into the canonical §7 contract while deferring all validation, conflict-resolution, and integration rules to an unspecified engineering dispatch; this creates an under-specified surface that can be extended later without another Panel cycle, undermining the very safety invariants (§7.6 regression guard, atomic ProductSSOT writes) the document claims to protect.

CA-16-A-v2-Q1.pick_text: REJECT — none of the listed options is acceptable as specified
CA-16-A-v2-Q1.rationale: Minimal envelope still lacks any tie to existing §7.6 or Self-Renewal invariants.

CA-16-A-v2-Q2.pick_text: REJECT — none of the listed options is acceptable as specified
CA-16-A-v2-Q2.rationale: Removing Step 1.5 without any ClearanceRecord linkage leaves recommendations untracked.

CA-16-A-v2-Q3.pick_text: REJECT — none of the listed options is acceptable as specified
CA-16-A-v2-Q3.rationale: Lifecycle states interact with unbounded defer windows and missing revert enforcement.

CA-16-A-v2-Q4.pick_text: REJECT — none of the listed options is acceptable as specified
CA-16-A-v2-Q4.rationale: 365-day bound and clamping rule are incompatible with §28 feedback timing.

perReviewer.overallNotes: All four questions inherit the same under-specification risk from the deferred schema.

questions.topic: CA-16-A v2 Q1 — Does Panel ratify the minimal §7 item #8 envelope (purpose-link optional, new cost object, new rollback object) with full schema deferred to engineering dispatch?

options.text: Ratify v2 as drafted (minimal envelope + 2 new fields; full schema deferred).
Ratify but require purpose_record_link mandatory IF `product_purpose` non-null (conditional mandatory).
Ratify with broader scope — full schema invariants (PA-1..PA-N) should be drafted in v2 itself.
Reject — proactive recs envelope should be canonical complete OR not canonical at all.

questions.topic: CA-16-A v2 Q2 — Does Panel ratify that proactive recommendations DO NOT participate in §11 Six-Step Clearance (Step 1.5 eliminated)?

options.text: Ratify but with Step 6.5 — recs surface AFTER Step 6 (Deploy/Promote) as post-deploy candidates.
Ratify with admin-dashboard-only requirement — recs live ONLY on dashboard.

questions.topic: CA-16-A v2 Q3 — Does Panel ratify the disposition lifecycle (open / accepted / rejected / deferred / implemented; carry-forward from v1)?

options.text: Ratify v2 as drafted (same lifecycle as v1).
Ratify with reopen state added — rejected recs may be reopened by admin with rationale.
Reject — lifecycle should be simpler: open / decided (no sub-states).
Defer entirely — lifecycle state machine belongs in engineering dispatch.

questions.topic: CA-16-A v2 Q4 — Does Panel ratify the per-product defer-window config (default 14 days; bounds [1,365]; admin-configurable)?

options.text: Ratify with stricter bounds — [7,90] instead of [1,365].
Ratify with admin role required for any value > 30 days; operator may set up to 30.
Reject — global fixed 14-day window simpler and sufficient.
